overall_assessment: Retain the proposed architecture. Persisted attempts, separate candidate and active credentials, channel-scoped encryption, durable provider ownership, a short transactional incoming boundary, bounded provider calls and DB-only listing form a coherent solution for ST-CON-01. All six earlier findings have substantial contractual resolutions. Two remaining interactions need a concrete contract and discriminating tests before approval: renewing an already verified Evolution pairing must revoke the old identity proof, and sender persistence must participate in the same identity/message reconciliation promised for outbound echoes. These are bounded gaps in the revised plan, not assertions that unimplemented changes have regressed the product.
correctness_position: Revise the two lifecycle/concurrency boundaries below. The initial onboarding, reauthorization, collision, ambiguity and incoming duplicate paths are otherwise described consistently. Preserve current public response and timeline contracts while correcting internal persistence; neither issue requires ST-CON-04, history import or a generic workflow platform.
security_position: The revised tenant predicates, server-side Meta resource proof, authenticated webhooks, one-use authorization, candidate isolation, AES-GCM/AAD and fail-closed decryption are sound. Initial Evolution input now has the required identity gate. The same gate needs an explicit trust-reset and stale-observation rule for RENEW, because a persisted proof from a previous pairing is not proof of the phone that has just scanned a new QR. Secret-free request logging and per-resource raw-event scoping remain implementation obligations under the existing contract, with focused harness notes below.
performance_position: Favorable, subject to the planned measurements. DB-only listing avoids provider fan-out; indexed attempt/credential/resource lookups and the message uniqueness constraint are appropriate. Three 10-second calls under a 45-second per-link lease bound a recovery round without holding a DB transaction during HTTP. The recommended fixes add short indexed/CAS operations and an indexed outbound upsert/reconciliation, rather than workers or an outbox. The small synthetic workload and pinned digest establish neither production capacity nor a continuous-health SLO.
elegance_position: Retain the small domain-specific state machine and explicit provider adapters. Make identity trust a property of the current pairing epoch, and give outbound message acceptance one consistent internal owner. Those changes remove implicit coupling. An in-memory echo cache, ad hoc query-before-insert exceptions, route-specific CSRF exceptions, global token fallback or a generic saga/vault/job framework would weaken this design.
structural_soundness_position: The BU remains the number, transports remain BU channels, and conversations remain keyed by BU/contact. Durable provider ownership and separate candidate/active credentials strengthen these boundaries. The two blockers are boundary omissions: channel existence/current generation versus current phone identity during renewal, and incoming uniqueness versus all writers of the same outbound message. Amend the strict expected-change reason for ConversationsService to admit the necessary internal persistence work while preserving DTOs, window rules and timeline behavior.
operational_fit_position: Local-first execution, a dedicated pinned Evolution runtime and storage, PostgreSQL 16, Node 22, a single principal-checkout writer, serial destructive suites and served-build attestation fit the declared scope. Meta eligibility/configuration, usable test assets, a real HTTPS callback, actual Evolution payload compatibility and real IN/OUT remain unknown. Their unknown state blocks the corresponding real-proof criterion, not honest planning. No legacy runtime adoption, Railway deployment or source promotion is authorized by this report.
test_quality_position: The planned PG E2E, real-backend browser lane, adapter/crypto tests, concurrency barriers, negative controls, source freshness and separate external proof are strong. REG-SEC-02 currently allows a duplicate OUT to pass because it requires only that an echo not become IN; REG-SEC-03 does not distinguish initial unverified pairing from renewing a previously verified instance. Add both discriminating sequences below. Existing fakes record only destination/text, so scoped-credential tests must observe the resource and credential identity at the external port without recording the secret. All assertions and results remain planned, not evidence of implemented safety.

blocking_findings.scope_classification: in-scope lifecycle clarification for SCOPE-04/05/09 and CON-04/REG-SEC-03; no new feature or generic infrastructure
blocking_findings.title: RENEW must invalidate the previous pairing's own-number proof before new input can be accepted

evidence.detail: INITIAL or RENEW uses the current link/generation, but the pairing action does not specify when an existing verified identity becomes untrusted.
The acceptance gate requires persisted verified own-number identity; it does not define a pairing epoch or how old same-instance observations are fenced during RENEW.
Current code routes solely by instance name; own phone is learned separately from connection.update at source line 94. No provider-carried local pairing generation is shown.
REG-SEC-03 covers input before initial confirmation; it does not start from an already verified channel and then renew pairing.

blocking_findings.concrete_failure: Start with the existing instance verified as phone X for BU X. An administrator requests RENEW and scans its QR with Y. If the new implementation merely adds the proposed persisted-identity check to the current routing, the old X proof remains true while Y's messages.upsert arrives before its connection observation. Y's content can therefore enter BU X. Merely clearing proof and allowing an old connection.update/open/wuid=X on the same instance to restore it leaves the same gap. A request-local lease or current generation captured when handling that old event does not prove which pairing produced it. This is a missing renewal contract, not a claim that the future implementation already behaves this way.
blocking_findings.why_now: Re-pairing/renewal is explicitly promised and tested in this story. The initial identity correction must hold throughout that lifecycle, including the period in which a previous proof already exists.
blocking_findings.recommended_correction: Freeze an explicit pairing trust epoch. Before any INITIAL/RENEW provider side effect, atomically invalidate the previous acceptance proof and fence pending identity/verification observations. Re-enable content only after current-epoch own-number evidence matches the canonical BU phone, with shared compare/fill-by-CAS behavior for an empty BU phone. A same-instance open event or old wuid observation cannot alone restore trust. Specify what positively ties the supported pinned provider's own-number proof to the renewed pairing; if that attribution cannot be established, retain PENDING_IDENTITY or use a generation-specific stable external instance identity and retire the old mapping. Do not present a locally assigned generation on an uncorrelated webhook as external proof. Maintain the chosen safe rejection/no-buffer policy.
blocking_findings.required_discriminating_test: With PostgreSQL and the real auth/domain boundary, begin from an accepted verified X channel, issue RENEW, and hold the external step behind a barrier. Assert proof is invalidated before that side effect. Deliver authenticated content for the new pairing before fresh own-number proof, a delayed old open/wuid=X event and an old verify completion; none may restore acceptance or persist content/raw, increment unread, publish or run a bot. Then prove ownPhone=Y produces quarantine and no effects. Repeat with a fresh matching X proof and replay the same message; exactly one accepted message results. A test that starts with an unverified channel does not discriminate this failure.

blocking_findings.scope_classification: in-scope correction needed to satisfy the newly explicit echo reconciliation contract; preserve public DTOs/windows/timeline
blocking_findings.title: The OUT sender and webhook echo must share the same acceptance key and persistence boundary

evidence.detail: The plan promises reconciliation of echo OUT with the persisted send by the same resource identity and external ID.
The strict expected-change reason permits ConversationsService to change only credential resolution, leaving its independent OUT insertion outside the proposed acceptance key.
Provider send precedes an unconditional message.create at source line 203; it currently stores externalId without a provider resource identity.
Provider fromMe events enter IncomingService as OUT, which independently creates Message.
REG-SEC-02 asserts echo does not become IN, which does not detect two persisted OUT rows.

blocking_findings.concrete_failure: The existing sender calls Evolution; Evolution delivers an authenticated fromMe echo with external ID E before the send promise resumes. The revised incoming path accepts OUT under resource R/E. The existing sender then inserts another OUT after the provider response. If only credential resolution is changed as permitted, its new resource-key columns remain absent/null and the incoming unique constraint cannot conflict; two timeline entries result. A sequential lookup for a previously persisted send also misses this echo-first ordering. If sender key columns instead become mandatory without reconciliation, the sender fails after a successful provider send. This is an existing send/echo race exposed by the new reconciliation promise, not an alleged implemented regression.
blocking_findings.why_now: The revised plan explicitly adds an identity/message key and promises echo reconciliation while retaining the send path. An internally coherent cutover needs all new writers of that same message identity to participate.
blocking_findings.recommended_correction: Permit the bounded internal OUT-persistence change in ConversationsService and any other actual sender. Resolve the authenticated channel resource identity for a send, populate it on new outbound records, and use one transactional create-or-reconcile path keyed by resource/external message ID for sender results and echoes. Define echo-first, sender-first and duplicate-echo outcomes, including retaining the human/Typebot author and returning the same persisted message to the sender. A unique collision must reconcile the existing message rather than fail a successfully completed send or insert a null-key duplicate. Keep network outside DB transactions, preserve public response/window contracts and do not add external-send retry or exactly-once claims.
blocking_findings.required_discriminating_test: Have the Evolution external-port stub deliver a real authenticated fromMe webhook inside enviarTexto, await its acceptance, and only then resolve the send with the identical external ID. Exercise the BFF and public sender paths that share the service. Assert one physical OUT row with the correct resource key, content and internal author, the returned message identity is that row, no IN/unread effect, and the existing response contract is preserved. Repeat sender-first and concurrently repeated echoes; a different resource using the same external ID remains independent. Add the equivalent check for another sender wherever that provider supports such echoes. Merely asserting direction=OUT is insufficient.
